lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: قَبْرِهِۦٓ is in the derivative form: قَبْر
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ق/ب/ر   q–b–r grave, tomb, cemetery, to bury, to entomb.

Of this root, 4 forms occur in 8 places in the Qur’an:
أَقْبَرَ ʾaqbara 1 time; قَبْر qabr 1 time; قُبُور qubūr 5 times and مَقَابِر maqābir 1 time.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
قَبْر qabr [n.; pl. قُبُور qubūr] tomb, grave

(22:7) وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِى الْقُبُورِ and surely God will raise those who are in the graves.

entries.label: أَقْبَرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
أَقْبَرَ ʾaqbara [v. IV, trans.] to cause to be buried, to hand over someone for burial, to cause burying to be the norm

(80:21) ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ then He causes him to die and be buried (or, made burial the norm for humankind).

entries.label: مَقَابِر
entries.definitionHtml:
مَقَابِر maqābir [pl. of n. مَقْبَرَةٌ maqbaratun] graves, burying places; cemetery, graveyard *

(102:2) حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ until you go into your graves [lit. until you visit the cemeteries].
